newsitem.title: CANADA: T. Eaton Co says restructuring plan on track.
newsitem.headline: T. Eaton Co says restructuring plan on track.

text.p: Canadian retailer T Eaton Co Ltd, currently under court protection from its creditors, said on Wednesday that its restructuring plan is on track.
"We feel very positive about the plan that is slowly coming to fruition," Eaton's chief financial officer John Anderson told reporters at a news conference.
Canada's fifth largest department store chain filed for creditor protection on February 27 and is expected to deliver a restructuring plan by mid-June.
Eaton's has said it may close up to 31 of its 85 stores.

Analysts have said several major American retailers are rumored to be eyeing the 127-year-old chain. The list of possible suitors included J.C. Penney Co Inc, Dayton Hudson Corp and Federated Department Stores Inc.
"The family will do what's best for all stakeholders," Anderson said.
He said the retailer is losing about C$2 million a week during this period, not including restructuring costs.
But he added retailers usually lose money during the first part of the year when sales are slow. Sales have dipped about one percent since Eaton's filed for creditor protection.
"When we table our restructuring plan, we'll find that the results are more favorable," Anderson said.
Eaton's is in the process of increasing its staff by 10 percent to boost sales, he said.
